parts.text: Which claim correctly compares those two prime factorisations?

options.text: Call the answer order of factors and stop there.
Having the same product $84$ is what creates the matching primes with the same repetitions.
$2\times 2\times 3\times 7$ and $2^{2}\times 3\times 7$ are the same prime factorisation; order and grouping do not change it.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Both writings list the same primes with the same repetitions, so they are one prime factorisation of $84$.

teacher.key_rationale: Unique prime factorisation cares about primes and multiplicities, not order or exponent notation. Naming order alone or reversing product as cause miss that.
